subject: Logic
title: Known vs Unknown Risks
description: A micro-lesson that makes Known vs Unknown Risks usable.

hook.text: Flipping a coin is risky. You know the odds. Starting a business? Risky—but you don't even know all the risks.

buildup.text: Risk means known probabilities. Uncertainty means the probabilities themselves are unknown.

discovery.text: Frank Knight made this distinction in 1921. Most real-world decisions live in uncertainty, not neat risk.

twist.text: Standard expected-value math works for risk. For true uncertainty, you need different strategies entirely.

climax.text: Under uncertainty, diversify, stay flexible, and cap your maximum downside rather than chasing optimal outcomes.

quiz.question: What is the difference between risk and uncertainty?
options: Risk has known probabilities; uncertainty does not
